note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl (T, 1312 rows, all attempt 0) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_rl_plain_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl (R, 1466 rows, attempts 0-2; attempt>0 restarts dropped), both in git. score_v3 as stored (int 0/1); no regrading. Main: each model's mean d over its own kept problems (>=1 finished S row n_new<8000 and >=1 finished L row n_new>=12000), statistic M_T - M_R. Alt reading: the same means restricted to problems kept for both models (paired). Bootstrap resamples the union of problem indices, each entry the pair (T rows, R rows), and recomputes both kept sets; a resample with an empty kept set would contribute 0 (unlikely). n = the smaller kept-problem count. refuted_by_met = statistic < 0.02 or either kept count < 5. Kept sets are likely small (problems need both a short and a long finished sample out of 4), so the interval may be wide; d is unweighted by row count.

Files: studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/math500_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl (2000 rows, attempt 0) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl (2041 rows, attempt>0 restarts dropped). Pooled sample-level precision of finished rows with n_new >= 8000 per model, Think-SFT minus RL. Alt reading: same pooled precisions restricted to problems where both models have at least one kept row. Bootstrap over the union of problem indices (pairs of row lists). n = the smaller kept-row count. refuted_by_met = statistic < 0 or either kept count < 20; an empty group prints refuted_without_number. On MATH-500 few answers reach 8k, so the kept rows may be few and concentrated on a handful of problems; long rows are a selected hard subset.

Files as in k=1 (hard328 Think-SFT cue and RL plain; attempt 0, first row per (problem_index, sample)). Pooled precision of finished rows with n_new < 4000, Think-SFT minus RL. Alt reading: restricted to problems where both models have a kept row (controls for different problem mixes among short answers). Bootstrap over problem pairs. n = smaller kept-row count. refuted_by_met = statistic < -0.06 or > 0.06. The two models' short-answer pools cover different problems (RL finishes short more often), so the main number mixes difficulty with model; the alt reduces that.

File: studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl (attempt 0, first row per (problem_index, sample)). Pooled precision of finished rows (cap_hit not true, finish_reason != 'length') with 14000 <= n_new <= 16383. Alt reading: upper bound 16384 inclusive (would only add finished rows at exactly the cap; probably identical). Bootstrap over problems that contribute kept rows. n = kept rows. refuted_by_met = statistic < 0.42 or fewer than 20 kept rows; zero kept rows prints refuted_without_number. Rows near the cap are a narrow band; whether n_new counts the final stop token could shift a few rows across 16383/16384.
